decisions.question: S121 found that ADR-001 item 9's one dart pub get --enforce-lockfile does not cure the exit 255 of dart run {package}:{executable} from a files/ directory on a workspace pub reads as stale (mtimes), and planned to run such a command as the package's bin script under the running dart with --packages. Accept the plan, or stop for the governance first?

options.label: Accept; route the ADR-001 items 7 and 9 restatement, nidana.model.md Scope (4) and nidana-checks@v1's Validation sentence to the end-of-node governance sweep
options.consequence: Implementation proceeds; the tool's form stays within item 7's text (it names the command, not how it runs); the governance's stated reason stays wrong until the sweep, which changes no code.

options.label: Insert hsdd-adr, hsdd-spec and hsdd-contract touches before implementing
options.consequence: Three governance steps now for wording that changes no code; delays the tool lane.

options.label: Run dart run as written
options.consequence: Twelve committed recorded invocations read exit 255 as their exit code whenever the workspace reads stale, which it does now.

decisions.chosen: Accept; route the ADR-001 items 7 and 9 restatement, nidana.model.md Scope (4) and nidana-checks@v1's Validation sentence to the end-of-node governance sweep
decisions.why: The experiments (file-cli-sets-plan K, M, N) show the failure and that no pub command refreshes the mtimes; the script form prints what dart run prints. Item 7 fixes the command's name, not its mechanism, so no governance text is contradicted; only the reason item 9 and Scope (4) give is wrong, and nidana.tooling's gates, the first to run these cases, come after the sweep.

decisions.question: The plan checks the restriction before PENDING for file and cli (nidana-checks@v1 has two producers, each gating on its own share), while nidana.model.6's behavior set checks PENDING first. Align the behavior set?

options.label: Keep both orders; record that every committed binding's packages exist by the first gate that runs it
options.consequence: No gate fails on the asymmetry today; a future binding whose suite slug is restricted out but whose package comes later would read PENDING under behavior.

options.label: Reorder behavior now
options.consequence: Reopens a merged, reviewed phase for no gate that needs it.

decisions.chosen: Keep both orders; record that every committed binding's packages exist by the first gate that runs it
decisions.why: Checked: flutter_navigation_executor_test.dart imports nidana_dart_navigation, created by nidana.navigation.1, on which nidana.flutter.1 depends; bus-api's bindings import the runtime that produces them. The behavior order is plan-reviewed (nidana.model.6 decision 5). The asymmetry goes to the report notes and the end-of-node sweep, where an ADR-001 touch can state one order.
